newsitem.title: USA: Viacom focuses Blockbuster on videos - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Viacom focuses Blockbuster on videos - WSJ.

text.p: Viacom Inc management is emphasizing Blockbuster's core video-rental business, retreating from a plan by the unit's former head to push into retailing, the Wall Street Journal said on Wednesday.
Blockbuster's former chief Bill Fields had opened test outlets which looked like convenience stores, selling soft drinks and junk food, the newspaper said.

The Journal quoted Viacom deputy chairman, Tom Dooley, as saying: "We want people to think of Blockbuster as a place to go to rent tapes. There was too much emphasis on retail at the expense of the core rental business."

Dooley was also quoted by the Journal as saying Viacom was watching the number people needed for Blockbuster's new headquarter operations in Dallas, and that the final number could be less than the 1,000 employees Fields saw.
